label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Size 2 cornice/loose avalanche came off the headwall while we approached another line. Winds were light to moderate and there is 25cm of low density snow available for transport.

reports.title: Bow Summit Observations
reports.comment: quick: Witnessed a natural size 1.5 loose dry up in the alpine. Heard multiple other natural avalanches in alpine terrain from treeline. Snow up to treeline was very thin. At treeline, there was a shallow snowpack (I'd say 30 cms on average). A sun crust was found at treeline on NE/E aspects overlayed with varying amounts of unconsoildated powder up to 15 cms. Still very rocky in the alpine. Wind …

reports.title: Bow Summit Slabs Forming - Alex Wright
reports.comment: snowpack: Hard shovel shear down 30cm. 15 cm Fist on top of 15 cm Four Finger density. This layer is skier triggerable.

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment: quick: HST 30, HS 50-80. 30cm of fresh snow (fist) on top of 20-50cm consolidated snow (4 finger). -3 at the car in the morning warming up to above freezing. Snow was noticeably more cohesive around 2pm

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment: quick: Still very early season conditions. Approximately 30 Cm of powder, and 50 Cm snowpack total. The base of the snowpack did a decent job protecting the skis from rocks - but sill some lurking sharks 🦈

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: There are shallow burrows rocks.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
avalanche: Around south shoulder. 40m to the climbers left of the small couloir that intersects with dog leg. Likely windloaded pocket in rock face that released and stepped down into storm snow on slopes below. Ran half way to the bench below. No picture of bigger slide. 

Also observed multiple remote triggers of SZ0.5 Storm Slabs BTL, in the large gulley headed back towards parking lot. (See at…

reports.title: Flower Couloir
reports.comment: avalanche: Triggered a small slab  ( Sunday ) on the way down Flower Couloir after deciding to turn around part way up. A Large amounts of slough were falling from the bowl above. A natural size 2 avalanche was triggered from the bowl above  Flower shorty after departing the Bowl. ￼

reports.title: Bow Summit Profile
reports.comment: quick: Bow Summit snow profile.

reports.title: Hwy 93 - Cirque Trees
reports.comment:
weather: Trace snow and some gusting winds. / snowpack: No observed failure in snowpack after compression testing. Snowpack consolidation was very even getting stiffer with depth.

Bottom 20cm was beginning to facet. The upper 70 cm appeared to be very nicely consolidating.

reports.title: The Stem and Bow
reports.comment:
quick: We went to try the stem today. There were a lot of avalanches in the Bow Summit area since/during that last storm. 

The Stem had lots of debris at the base and was quite wind hammered. It was hard to hold an edge skinning up the lower bit with no ski pen. The winds were very strong and the skiing seemed very unappealing so we went to ski the normal stuff off the shoulder at Bow. Of note wa…

reports.title: Bow Summit ski resort
reports.comment:
quick: Great day at Bow Summit ski resort with the other 100 people there! Lots of people on the parkway in general. 

Visible wind loading on lee slopes. Wind was SW and loading the E/NE facing slopes. The regular laps in the gullies were good with high quality snow for November. 

See snowpack tab for pit info. And yes, Backcountry YYC fans, we filled the pit afterwards.

Other misc beta: the pa…

reports.title: Katherine Lake Ridge
reports.comment: snowpack: No crust. 65 to 55 F 55 to 35 4F 35 to 10 1F 10 to 0 4F

reports.title: Puzzle peak
reports.comment: quick: Went to go ski puzzle peak but it was pretty cloudy and snowy with limited vis so just skied some mellow trees below instead. On the ski out we saw an old natural avi that failed on the basal facets (15-20cm) above ground. Snowpack felt stable and saw no other signs of instability. We did see some wind effect in spots at treeline and I can imagine it’s more widespread up high. Didn’t run in…

reports.title: Dolomite shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Nice, supportive snowpack. Thin coverage, but adequate for travel below treeline. No new avalanches observed.

reports.title: Bow Falls Area
reports.comment:
quick: Ice climbing in the Bow Falls area, ended up climbing the flows right of Bow falls for 3 pitches up to WI4. Didn't climb Bow due to spindrift or Gorby's due to spindrift and cornice failure/formation above.

Parking was plowed, lake not frozen enough to cross (open water visible in spots). / avalanche: Multiple immature (soft) cornice failures, especially nearby Gorby Falls. Cornice line is…

reports.title: Crystal Ridge Frontside
reports.comment: quick: Great day skiing up to Crystal Ridge Pass. The pass didn't appear to have slid on the November 5th layer yet and is a lovely combo of bony rock and wind slab so we elected to ski back down the front side. Skiing is great in areas that are protected from the wind and 5-10cm of powder on a supportive crust on windward faces. The supportive crust settled once on the way up when the two of us w…

reports.title: Gorby Falls - Cornice Avalanche
reports.comment:
avalanche: Witnessed a size 2 avalanche due to a wind loaded cornice breaking free. 

Avalanche was over Gorby Falls. 

Lots of spindrift and wind loading today. 
Cornices noticeably larger by the end of the day. 

We climbed the middle line of Bow Falls. 
Good climbing up to WI4. 
Hero ice. Some shell ice pulling over bulges.

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: Strong winds overnight, moderate with strong gusts in the morning.  Stayed clear of windloaded terrain and overhead hazard.

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Skied Helen Shoulder today. Seemed like 10-15cm overnight. The Parkway was surprisingly slow with only a handful of other parties all the way to Bow Summit. The winds on the ridge at the top of the burn were very strong. We had to take a knee to transition. Wind was predominately out of the north. At the car there was minimal wind and it was quite warm -1c when we left and returned. In hind…

reports.title: Pointless Gully
reports.comment:
quick: P1 was very wet but overall decent conditions and quite fat (WI3).
P2 was wet and had some difficult conditions but good screws if you worked for them (WI4).

Heavy drifting along the lakeside trail. Travel to and from the route was very difficult and length once off the flats and normal trail. Very deep snow, hard even with skis on.

reports.title: Dolomite shoulder
reports.comment: quick: We skied Dolomite Shoulder, morning was calm and clear at the base and got colder and windy through the day. Stuck to the trees up to the shoulder and skinned up the very wind affected ridgeline. Above 2300m, snow was wind swept and scoured on the ridge, hard pack skiing down but hit no rocks. Below 2300m snow was deep and powdery in the trees, with great turns and coverage. Snow got wet/he…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Surprisingly quiet at Bow Summit for a Saturday. Great skiing. Powder in the trees and sheltered areas but wind affected and firm above treeline. HS 85cm on SE aspect at ~2270m. Light SW wind. Partially cloudy with light snow beginning at 12:30 and increasing into the afternoon. We did not observe any avalanches or signs of instability. Rocks exposed where snowpack was thin especially in th…

reports.title: Helen shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Great day up in the Helen shoulder bowl area. The day started off with good vis and slowly turned to a cloudy day with light flurries. Skied a lap lookers left of the burnt trees and then 2 more further left in the bowl on lightly treed slopes. Found windslabs in the alpine and ski cut a small convexity at the top of our first line that was obviously loaded with no results. Snow wasn’t grea…

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment: quick: The facets causing the persistent slab layer at the very bottom of snow pack seem better bonded than the previous week. A newer weak layer roughly 50cm deep failed/ collapsed after the 6th shoulder tap.

reports.title: Heavy Day in Crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: Snowfall continued throughout the day in the glades with light winds. New snow amounted to 10-15 cm on previous unconsolidated powder. Terrain of choice today included trees and slopes <25°

Avalanches were heard releasing in the distance throughout the day. 

A quick & dirty pit on a North aspect at treeline showed reactivity of 2 storm snow layers in the easy range. Deeper layers were rea…

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment: quick: It was dumping on the parkway today, at 1cm/hour in the morning, and ramping up to 3cm/hour by mid afternoon.  We stuck to slopes under 25 degrees without overhead hazard.  We noticed some cracking and propagation on wind slab layer below the storm snow above treeline, though we weren't on anything steep enough to slide.  We heard some slides in the distance, but with heavy cloud cover we c…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Submitting on behalf of my AST1 Students:
-Avalanche path that faces 93N highway half way between Bow Summit and Jimmy Jr Shoulder (ENE aspect) slid to size 3 taking out a few mature trees and reaching the flat meadow.  Light too flat to see crown/start zone.  Estimate it occurred on Dec2/3
-Nov5th Crust/facets (weak layer) felt near bottom of snowpack at 2200m
-Around 2cm new snow fell fro…

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak, Jimmy Jr...weekend round-up
reports.comment: quick: On December 4 we ascended to benchy terrain at TL on the NE shoulder of Jimmy Jr to assess conditions at TL and have a look into the alpine. Reaching the base of Jimmy Jr bowl we observed the debris pile of a large natural avalanche that occurred during the last storm, which removed trees up to 20cm in diameter. The new snow was becoming wind affected above 2300m, and had an upside-down fee…

reports.title: Helen shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Crusty up to 2100 but not bad above.  Main west bowl  looked heavily wind affected.   ENE 2350 (backside of the burn) 115 HS , 7 Uneven break in storm, 12 SP on Nov 15
,22 SP on Nov 5. Said nope and stuck to mellow with aspect glades which rode alright, bit heavy but no significant affect.

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Great skiing on skier's right of the bowl.Ski pen in upper bowl 30 - 40cm. Somewhat busy with 2 large groups of 8+ people plus a few group of 2-3

Witnessed the result of a class 3 which started high up on the cliff at the top of the bowl filled the entire left side of the bowl all the way to the trees at the bottom. Several trees broken. Likely happened with the previous 48 hrs near the en…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Many parties out at Crowfoot Glades on Sunday. Conditions were pretty good, with soft powder at higher elevations. Dug a pit and did not note any instabilities. It seemed like the new storm snow had bonded fairly well with below layers. Slight wind effect on isolated features typically on N/NE aspects. We avoided overhead hazards from the nearby rock face and stuck closer to the treed ridge…

reports.title: Bow Hut route
reports.comment: quick: Went into Bow Hut Saturday and came out Sunday. Lake was suspicious so we went around. Coverage on the whole route is very good for this time of year. The canyon is filled in well, only one minor crossing. Lots of debris slid into the canyon during the storm making it seem a bit safer. Crust found up to 2200m. Snow was largely wind affected everywhere and slow skiing sticky cold snow. Nothi…

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Tree line and above very wind affected. Also alpine areas with thin snowpack. Alpine area felt sketchy with multiple wind slabs and cornice development. We did make it to the top of the ridge. Due to the sketchy wind slabs we had to cross, we decided to stick to our skin trails on the way down. Below tree line the runs were pretty skied out, but still some areas in between with deep powder …

reports.title: Mike Short
reports.comment: quick: Good day, we found 5cm of dust on crust at lake level, with the crust getting deeper as we climed.  The curst disappeared just below treeline

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: Good Skiing in the alpine, traversed into the main slide path, which riding quality quickly changed to dust on crust and hard pack luge trail to trailhead. Creek crossing required some special attention but manageable. Road was a skating rink. / avalanche: Observed a couple suspected older natural windslab avalanches in the alpine, and one more recent sz 0.5 skier triggered in the upper alp…

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment: quick: Dug a pit at edge of treeline, 90cm depth, layers seemed pretty consolidated until the bottom ~5cm basal facets. Top was a bit mushy but nothing deep failed during column test.

reports.title: Bow Summit study plot profile
reports.comment: quick: Bow Summit study plot profile.

reports.title: Jimmy Simpson
reports.comment:
quick: Saw a lot of wind affect out there, in different directions or on different aspects compared to what I normally see. In some areas it seemed like the wind had been S/SW. 
Rain crust present to 2200m. Above that there was either wind slab or soft powder depending on which 5ft segment you were looking at. It actually skied pretty well, but I wouldn't have wanted to go into steep terrain. Ther…

reports.title: Helen Burn
reports.comment: quick: A good day on mellow slopes. 65cm base at the top of the burn, 100 at the bottom. Lots of crossloading into skiers left green trees / snowpack: Dam basal facits.

reports.title: Natural avalanche crowfoot glades
reports.comment: avalanche: Natural avalanche observed near the north facing slope of the overhead hazard near the base off crowfoot glades. Possible trigger from rockfall that was heard from a distance.

reports.title: Crowfoot glades avalanches
reports.comment:
avalanche: Saw multiple relatively small size (1-1.5) natural avalanche coming from the alpine face to the west of crowfoot glades. Most stopped in the “valley” between the alpine face and treeline. 

However, one notable exception was a size 2.5 that ran full length (all the way down to the drainage/terrain-trap between crowfoot glades and and the end of the moraine bowl). This was a near miss fo…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Snowing lightly until mid-afternoon. -12C in the a.m. warming to -10C during the day. Probing around noticed the rain crust (thick) ~40cm down at the base of the glades (1960m). HS (Height of Snow) ~155cm down low. Very thin or no crust up top (2240m). Surprised to see little cornicing or snow coming off the headwall after the MINs from Saturday. Confirmed the sloughing (dry loose) problem …

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment:
snowpack: ECT at around 2250 m on SE aspect at ~1:30 pm Sunday. 

Dug my pit on a steep convex slope, and found 215 cm of snow. Depth was highly variable and in some other places showed less than 60 cm. 

Two failures, first occurred after 3 easy taps 30 cm down. Resistant planar failure. 

Second failure occurred after 9 easy taps 50 cm down. Resistant planar failure. 

In both cases the snow abo…

reports.title: OXO Puzzle Peak Ramp
reports.comment: quick: OXO Puzzle Peak Ramp wind effected/wind crust. Some sections of ramp 15-25cm wind deposited pow on top of supportive wind crust. No recent avalanches or signs of instability noted. Did not hit any sharks. Excellent powder skiing on exit through trees/benches to creek.

reports.title: Crowfoot Pass
reports.comment:
quick: 20-40 cm of low density storm snow up to TL. Non reactive hard slab in Alpine up to the pass with pockets of low density snow in sheltered alpine features.

Evidence of cornice fall off BowCrow Peak

Great skiing at TL and below.

reports.title: Helen shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Good skiing in open glades BTL. Wind affected at TL in exposed terrain. Dug a pit in the burn. HS 80cm at 2250m. A bit shallower than expected. CTH21 RP on the nov 5 facets. This result and the thin snowpack made us wish we had stayed in the glades along the shoulder.

reports.title: Katherine Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Calm and mostly cloudy today, clearing around dusk, 10-15cm last night into this morning. Snowpack felt stable but did not examine below the surface.

reports.title: Dog Leg
reports.comment: quick: Deep snow and deep wallowing up dogleg. Snow was increasing density as far as we could probe. About 10cm fresh over night. Boot packing up there is a big hollow spot that would make a good bivy cave. Lots of loose snow but nothing felt slabby.

reports.title: Birdfeeder
reports.comment: quick: Profile on E side of Crowfoot Mountain at 2250 m.

reports.title: Vulture Peak avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Size 3.5 to 4 natural avalanche occurred off the North side of Vulture Peak. We suspect this occurred 3 to 5 days ago. The avalanche failed on the basal facets/depth hoar at the glacier ice interface. Debris covered the normal Bow Hut approach route and ran down as far as the top of the canyon leading up to Bow Hut.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: avalanche: Observed size ~2 avalanche come off the Bowcrow headwall.

reports.title: Bow Jr.
reports.comment: quick: Checked out Jimmy Jr. Saturday. Visibility was low low low. Lots of tracks from Friday. Noticed while skinning up to the top some fresh overhead releases from steep alpine areas that fell next to the headwall on lookers left.  We opted to cut it short, and pushed over to the slide paths further north and ski the avvy paths. Great skiing to be found from the edge of the alpine down in to the…

reports.title: Cirque area
reports.comment:
quick: Completed a link up of the sugar cube couloir and cirque peak north couloir. Excellent skiing with some minor sluffing in the sugar cube. Rap necessary for the entry. Large cornices developing in other areas of crystal ridge. 

Cirque peak ramp was largely wind blown and the last 100 m needed to be bootpack. 2 raps required for the north couloir as it was quite thin. Back glacier was well f…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Couple laps in Jimmy Jr Bowl area. Heard some big whumps when skinning near a cross-loaded convex rolls at the top of the slide path lookers right of the bowl. The main bowl skied a bit punchy but still soft. North aspect off the shoulder lookers left was great skiing once lower and sheltered, hard and punchy wind affect near the top. Popped a small wind skin(knife hardness, 5cm deep, 5m pr…

reports.title: Cirque sub peak
reports.comment: quick: December 20th we skied the north and south bowls near Cirque Peak. A cold start to the day with temps around -25c at 9:30. Around noon we were in t-shirts and an inversion was evident. Both slopes skied well with cold and dry pow and slightly variable wind effect. West facing slopes are typically very thin and a light step was required to navigate  the rocks. There was evidence of cornice f…

reports.title: Bow Hut approach
reports.comment:
quick: Cold day as one would expect. Recent storm snow was reactive. 

We turned around from the hut part way through the canyon due to a combination of open water and sluffing of the recent storm snow. Making crossing above the river dangerous. 

One in our party did slide a few meters into the water on the storm slab, resulting in a wet boot. He hiked out of the creek and we decided it was to un…

reports.title: Dolomiti shoulder
reports.comment:
weather: Thursday Dec 30.  
13:00 hrs at 2230 m: -19, calm, thin cloud on peaks and in valley bottom.   
14:00 hrs at 2500 m: -24, light SW wind, ice crystals. / snowpack: Thurs Dec 30, 13:00.  Easy hand shears on way up above ~ 2150 m on a planar layer, though unconsolidated.  
Quick pit at 2230 m on SE aspect on 30 deg slope:
HS 165;  165-140cm Fist;  CT4 uneven P @ 140cm;  140-110cm 4F-1F;  CT1…

reports.title: Crystal ridge
reports.comment: quick: Good skiing. No signs of instability noted other than loose sluffing on steep cliffy terrain across the highway.

reports.title: Mt. Jimmy Simpson
reports.comment: quick: See comments in snowpack. Slab avalanche refers to skier triggered avi observed on opposite side of valley on Observation Mountain that ran very far in adraw to tree line / snowpack: 30cm ski pen came to rest on a 10cm thick crust. Below crust was weak layers of variable snow and facets that would not support the weight of my ski pole when slight downward pressure was applied. Pole went in …

reports.title: Helen Shoulder - Trees
reports.comment: quick: Stayed in low angle terrain and stopped just before getting out of treeline. Avalanche condition were stable in the trees did not venture out of treeline

reports.title: First outing in warmer 2022 weather
reports.comment: quick: There was evidence of older avalanches higher on the mountain that were partially covered in snow. More evidence of old avalanches across the valley above tree line. / weather: The occasional gust did knock snow off of the trees

reports.title: Jimmy Slide Paths
reports.comment: quick: Good snow found in roadside slide paths. Two recent avalanches observed across the valley in the area of Observation Sub Peak as well as two small avalanches above the slide paths, both off the steep cliffy bench in the alpine. Debris didn't trigger anything on slopes below. Multiple groups with ~10+ people seen in Jimmy Simpson bowl. An avalanche had run from lookers left couloir feature w…

reports.title: Bow Summit AST2
reports.comment: quick: Did a wee lap at Bow Summit and noticed old wind slab underfoot covered by about 5-10cm new snow at BLT/TR. No signs of instability. We avoided steep and wind loaded features staying in the trees. / weather: We mostly stayed below treeline for the majority of the day doing beacon practice. The wind was consistently moderate/strong SW/W throughout the day at TR/BLT with 1cm/hr snow accumulat…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Skied 4 laps in the various tree chutes. First lap we ventured in to more open trees at tree line and found ski quality to be terrible. The next three laps we skied the lower short slide paths about 1km south of the parking lot. Ski quality was top notch, with no signs of instability. 

We witnessed a rescue up valley as a solo hiker had fallen in a hole the afternoon prior and nearly froze…

reports.title: Observation Glades test profile
reports.comment: snowpack: Found 125cm in an open glade amoungst the last significant trees on the rib above our snow study plot. Overall a weak and well-faceted snowpack with only the snow from before the middle of November providing any real strength. It seems apparent that the cold temperatures from the entire month of December have really driven the facet process in these thin snowpack areas common to this sid…

reports.title: Dolomite shoulder
reports.comment:
snowpack: Quick pit for some layer ID and testing

Surface hoar up to 2cms in open areas in BTL and TL on most aspects and elevations we observed, on our short venture up to the edge of the alpine it looked like the wind had knocked down any surface hoar development.

Generally solid upper and mid pack, top 20cms was a layer of fist DFs over another 12cms of 4F snow, from there down to 115cms we f…

reports.title: Grand daddy stair master
reports.comment: quick: -13.5 @ the car park at 8am. -4 about half way up at noon. Firm snow but not terrible skiing by any means at TL and above. (Better BTL) Hard to moderate hand shears at 10cm and 30cm down. 1F ,1F+. Loose dry up to 1.5 in the last 24h. Cornice chunks mixed with debris from extreme terrain. Turned around just over half way up the couloir, the forecasted WSL was present and over our risk tolera…

reports.title: Grand Daddy Couloir
reports.comment:
avalanche: After transitioning to bootpacking and going up 10m in the Grand Daddy Couloir, a sluff avalanche fell from the right wall.
One skier managed to dodge the avalanche by taking cover over the pillar.
The other skier got caught in the avalanche and got dragged to the bottom of the runway. No burial and no serious injuries. Only lost a pole, ski strap and 2 disclocated shoulders. / incident…

reports.title: Patterson Area
reports.comment:
snowpack: Short day exploring treeline terrain near Mt Patterson. We observed whumpfing from BTL up to about 1900 m in open sparsely teeed areas. Pole probing suggested 2 crusts at about 60 and 80 cm depth with underlying facets to ground. 
Above 1900 m, observed wind effect on exposed ridges. Sheltered skiing was excellent with 5-10 cm on supportive temperature/wind crust. No visible signs of ava…

reports.title: Mosquito Creek - Couloir Avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: I made about 5 turns from the top of the couloir and tucked over to the side to video the second skier in what I thought was a safe location. Around turn 3 the second skier triggered a slab which carried me ~200m, there was a decrease in the angle of the slope and I was backstroking like crazy and slowed while the avalanche carried on another 150-200m in the fan. It may have been a wind…

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Headed up Crystal Ridge for a few laps today. We climbed all the way to the ridge and looked over at Helen's lake, everything in the alpine was very wind effected and just starting to get wet on the south and west aspects by the end of the day. But there was good turns to be had on the short pitches and in between the trees, still some nice snow especially in the shade or near shady spots. …

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Uneventful day with temps ranging between -6c to 0 c.  Most of the treeline has been hammered by wind.  Some fresh 15 cm turns hidden in the trees.  The area is skied up and wind blown crust everywhere there isn’t tree protection.  Needs some new snow.

No instability noticed in the Alpine the 4 hrs we were there.

reports.title: Sub Observation Peak
reports.comment: quick: Went up through the creek (instead of climbers right) which worked well due to the thick snowpack BTL. It’s another story in the alpine: all the snow has been blown off to SK! Went up via the Sub Peak - Cirque pass, had to take skis off for 100m over the broad NE ridge before the glacier (glacier is receding fast OMG). We were careful avoiding steep slopes where the hard wind crust turned i…

reports.title: Glades
reports.comment: quick: Sweet easy turns for a quick afternoon ski

reports.title: Dolomite Curcuit
reports.comment:
quick: Skied dolomite circuit.

Size 2 avalanche debris in the runouts of Dolomite when going up the creek, but it was at least days old, and stopped in the upper run-outs.  We observed two cornice failures that caused size 2.5 to 3 avalanches.  East and South aspects in the alpine.  

We experienced no cracking or whoomphing.  The snow in the alpine and exposed areas at treeline varies from lizar…

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment:
quick: 2/3 kind of day - variable wind affected snow, but good company and great views. 

Fun time boot packing pillow lines at the end of the day down low.

reports.title: Wapta icefields
reports.comment: avalanche: Toured to the Wapta icefields with plans to do mt.Thompson. A windstorm started to pick up and lash the area as we were at Bow Hut. We turned around at the ridge adjacent to the onion but the slopes we had taken up were now very wind loaded. We safely made it down from the hut without triggering anything but once we entered the drainage pass closer to Bow lake we accidentally triggered …

reports.title: Cirque Peak Traverse
reports.comment: quick: No whumpfing or cracking - prob’ly cause it was so damn rock solid all the way around. A few moments gave us pause to put on ski crampons (got my money’s worth of use today), take slopes one at a time in several spot to manage risk, despite no observations of activity. Glad viz was excellent. Descent down cirque was wretched firm. Despite apparently stable slopes, I wouldn’t repeat for a ve…

reports.title: Jimmy Junior
reports.comment: quick: Good day before the warmth got to the snow. Skied 1 lap in Jimmy Junior Bowl before the rapid temp rise and sun. Skied 2 laps in a drainage to the south. Snow got progressively heavier as the day went on. Saw storm clouds developing to the north and had intermittent snow a t less than 1cm per hour.

reports.title: West Nile + Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Awesome day skiing west Nile. Stability was good so we headed up towards the southern ridge of bow peak. 

Small cracks coming from storm/wind slabs heading towards the ridge. Small point release slugging observed but not running far at all. 

Skiing was deep and floaty in the alpine and soft in the slide paths.  

West Nile is fairly tracked out now

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades - Natural into Moraine Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Cool day exploring Crowfoot glades into the upper reaches of the bench. Snow not great, warming above 0 into high elevations. Witnessed a natural as shown in pics, described in Avalanche tab. Start zone was not in accessible terrain but it ran from overhead into Moraine bowl. / avalanche: Witnessed a loose dry natural class 2 from a distance while skinning out from Crowfoot glades across th…

reports.title: Grand Daddy Couloir
reports.comment: quick: A perfect day skiing Grand Daddy couloir. A hard boot pack to get up rewarded us with a beautiful descent. We transitioned 50m from the very top once the snow was chest deep and we couldn't go up anymore. There was also some wind slab building near the top. One to remember!

reports.title: Bow Summit study plot
reports.comment: snowpack: Bow Summit study plot - Feb 10, 2022. Snow depth 132 cm. Thin sun crust just below surface snow. No significant shears found in tests. Jan 30 layer unreactive in this spot. Dec 2 crust/facets still present and weaker than the surrounding snow.

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Skied Little Crowfoot. The wicked wind has had her way with the alpine. Windward slopes are scoured to bare rock & the glacier was a mess of hammered sastrugi on gear (see photo 1). Ski pen 0. Foot pen 0. Thick, supportive crust on all aspects. Sheltered Northerly slopes near treeline held good snow, but BTL often boasted a breakable melt freeze crust. Fast travel overall. Ski crampons are …

reports.title: Cirque Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Not great snow conditions, but fun day to walk up a rocky ridge and rappel into a north facing couloir (35m).  Very large cornices kept us traversing far away from slide paths. 

Highlights weren’t in the riding conditions, however on south facing slopes we did observe: two white-tailed ptarmigans, a spruce grouse, a hairy woodpecker, countless lynx tracks, and fresh grizzly bear tracks. We…

reports.title: Dolomite Traverse
reports.comment: quick: Good day on the dolomite traverse. Bring ski crampons for the initial ascent. Hard and crusty snow for entire traverse. Fast travel on the way out. Saw no avalanches, mild temps. Road were very icy, saw cars in the ditch.

reports.title: Jimmy Simpson Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Good day in Jimmy Simpson Bowl. We skied two laps of the entire length of the bowl with two other parties. The area has been refreshed with 10 - 15cm of new snow which sat on a layer of much firmer snow. New snow was softer lower down in the bowl and became firmer higher up as it was exposed to the wind. Pockets of powder and crust could be found throughout the bowl which caused the snow to…

reports.title: Cirque
reports.comment: quick: Fully refreshed from last few days of snow. ~20cm ski penetration up through to treeline. Some wind affected areas and crust still evident into the alpine, so skiing was kept to treeline and below where skiing was softer. No stability issues observed.

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment:
quick: Good refresh with 30cm light powder. No wind effect below treeline. Snow pack 175cm at 2200m. Supportive layers beneath new snow. Several groups out today. ~20 skiers. Still loads of untouched snow to ski. 

Temps - 10 all day. Overcast with S1 in the morning. Lightened up mid to late afternoon.

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Skiied the couloir left of Jimmy Jr Bowl. Powder was approx 2ft deep in the couloir, bomber crust underneath made bootpacking easy and safe. Only concern was sluff control, which turned out to be less of an issue than expected. Observed a 1.5 avalanche at the headwall of the bowl. / avalanche: Sluffalanche triggered by loose snow falling from the headwall of Jimmy Jr Bowl, picking up more d…

reports.title: Nosseeum Summit Ridge bowl
reports.comment: quick: Skied the SE facing bowl off the Summit ridge. Mixed bag of wind affect and sun crust on the way up. Found an isolated pocket of 20cm thick wind slab on a small sw facing pitch just above tree line that produced shooting cracks and other isolated pockets of 5cm wind slab in the alpine on the same aspect. Seemed to be developed more from wind affect than actual loading. All of this was sitti…

reports.title: Bow Summit North Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Easy day on the north shoulder of Bow Summit. Avg 20-30cm of new F snow, with pockets of 4F wind slab. CTH 24 (SP) down 70, 35° NE aspect on an open alpine slope @ 2250m.

reports.title: Bow Falls
reports.comment:
quick: 80 km/hr winds started howling near the top of the climb, bailed off a thread just short of the top. Severe spindrift was observed.

Ice quality was mediocre/poor. Brittle and dinner platey. Could benefit from some warming / traffic. Lots of cleaning required

reports.title: Patterson
reports.comment:
quick: Patterson right couloir had sloughed earlier in the week leaving a bit of a gnarly crust on the surface that wasn't particularly fun to ski. The fan skied well.

High westerly winds observed at the end of the day (see picture) with numerous spindrifts off the alpine faces above the run. / snowpack: Bootpack was crusty on surface but easy to break through to 4 finger snow (faceted?) below. M…

reports.title: West Nile Alpine & Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Left truck at 9:45 AM with overcast, -7 C and negligible wind in the valley.  Moved up on to main Avi path - lower elevations skied up with hard pack.  Above the TL - no visible tracks and a 10 mph W / SW wind moving snow around.  Snow showers all day with about a total accumulation of 5 cm.  Not much for hard wind slab but certainly pockets of fresh wind deposits.  Skied down for 250 m.

B…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Venturing much beyond the treeline not worth it, snow was wind affected and hard. Treeline and below held tons of powder and more was falling. Area near the parking lot fairly tracked out but everything around the gully and south was awesome, deep untouched powder.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Couple of laps in the glades. Wind was blowing above tree line which had started to form the new snow into slabs. Ski quality was a little crusty until you got into really sheltered spots. Sun kept teasing its arrival, but never appeared.

No signs of instability today.

reports.title: Cirque Peak N Coulior
reports.comment: quick: Skied the N Coulior of Cirque yesterday (March 5). We were able to skin to just below the false summit then switched to bootpacking. After tagging the summit we completed 2 x 30m rappels to reach snow. The second anchor is about 2 body lengths off the deck and required a bit of dry tooling to reach. The coulior skied quite well but short. We found a bit of reactive wind slab at the coulior …

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl / Slide Paths
reports.comment:
quick: Skiied the two runouts climbers right of Jimmy Jr Bowl, then did a third lap dropping into the bowl from the North. CT15 planar fracture at 45cms, suspect that this was the persistent slab reported in the forecast. 

Snow skiied excellent, did not feel unstable and no issues throughout the day. Several other groups on the mountain. Despite lots of sun, surface snow in the area stayed light …

reports.title: Patterson Via Delta Creek
reports.comment:
quick: Up Patterson yesterday. Temp crust to around 2000m. We did find the Feb 16th PWL but only in steep solar aspects and observed no whumpfing. Elsewhere 10-30cms of soft snow from summit to valley bottom showing no signs of  wind effect and no slab properties at all. Made for fantastic skiing top to bottom maybe with the exception of the top 100m where the midpack was nonexistent. 

Temps arou…

reports.title: Helen-Kate Ridge
reports.comment: quick: 5-6cm of snow in the surface. Some wind affected snow in alpine. Lots of sun and the snow was becoming wet towards the end of the day. Some snowballing below the cliffs.

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Went for a nice walk up Little Crowfoot today. Found some nice powder in the Ferris Glacier area and down to the canyon. The stay started around -12 but quickly warmed, -2 on return to the parking lot. Winds picked up in the afternoon with obvious transport off the icefields to lee holding areas. Suspect for new wind slabs tomorrow? A few recent sluffs off extreme solar terrain noted but no…

reports.title: Mt Patterson Central
reports.comment: quick: 8am start. -16°c at the car. Fast approach to reach the base from the roadside crossing the river. Solid and stable conditions for most of the boot pack. 5cm wind crust in the top third with soft consolidated storm snow beneath. Topped out with no apparent wind which made it feel like spring transitioning in the sunshine. Some minor dry loose sluff on the descent but was easily managed. Top…

reports.title: Crowfoot avalanche
reports.comment: quick: Seen from the road.

reports.title: Mt Patterson SE couloir
reports.comment: quick: Had a look up Patterson SE coulior feeling hopeful that a tight feature would be a good choice for the day. Coulior itself had flushed a few days ago and had a nice 5-10cm refresh over top. Flush had originated from 3/4 up and once above into the more open alpine pocket we started to find buried wind slab over top facets. 10-15 of low density powder with a thin wind skiff on top, sat over 1…

reports.title: Bow Summit Study Plot full profile
West Nile
reports.comment:
quick: No result from CT. East aspect, 33 degree, snow depth 250cm, 2160 elevation.
40cm from top was the suncrust layer which is starting to bond with recent snow.

reports.title: Crowfoot Couloir and Fan Yoyo Laps
reports.comment: quick: Skiied Crowfoot Couloir today. Temps around -5 with heavy clouds and light flurries throughout the day. Solid boot packing up the couloir with periodic spin drift coming off all walls. We experienced one significant sluff from a suspected cornice failure over the top of the couloir that got our tail between our legs! Overall skiied well with the crust barely noticeable. The fan below also s…

reports.title: Noseeum Creek
reports.comment: avalanche: Notable wind and snowfall during approach to the head wall. Our group of three observed a naturally triggered avalanche on a SE facing couloir, most likely a windslab release on the solar aspect overhead. We turned around and went to crowfoot glades where the snow quality was excellent in the trees. We also heard a large avalanche while at crowfoot.

reports.title: 93 North
reports.comment:
quick: Snowing all day, more heavily in the afternoon, limited visibility.
A few shooting cracks observed at treeline in wind affected areas.

reports.title: 45cms if wind slab sitting on facets
reports.comment:
quick: 45cm of wind slab sitting on facets

Multiple cornice releases over4days of wind and snow

Mt Balfour area

reports.title: Dolomite traverse
reports.comment: quick: Great day out on Dolomite traverse! Boot top pow was mostly untouched by wind, however the sun made intermittent appearances and acted fast. Moist snow in the final tree decent to the highway, and we noticed slabs that had been triggered below sun exposed cliffs. Slabs were size 1-2 including one that ran over ski tracks off of Puzzle Peak.

reports.title: Helen shoulder
reports.comment: quick: More snow than expected in parking lot. We broke trail along the summer trail. Ski pen 25cm minimum. The day started off colder but as we gained elevation throughout the day, the temp increased to -2 and we observed moist surface snow on north and south aspects. / avalanche: Observed what seemed to be a slab avalanche on steep alpine slope of neighbouring peak SW of Bow lake. It stopped on …

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Awesome day out at Crowfoot, lots of breaking trail in deep powder and fantastic skiing. We saw no signs of instability where we skied. 
However, there was lots of soft cornice failures and dry loose coming off of steep rocky aspects in the alpine.
Probed 270cm at 2135m, 15-20cm of light fresh snow on top of recent storm snow. Foot pen over 45cm / avalanche: Lots of avalanches, soft cornice…

reports.title: Flower Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Our plan for the day was to ski the flower couloir and the petal. As we skinned up the approach we notice 2 natural wind slabs in the vicinity of the couloir. One on N and one on NE. The largest one (see picture) looked fresh, maybe from the previous day? The other one was about 20m right of the couloir exit (size 1). 
We also experienced some shooting cracks on the way up. Considering the …

reports.title: Sugar Cube Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Skiied the sugarcube couloir today, was full of powder and ended up being very stable. 

First test was CT 11, 16 at 20cm and 40cm depths at the toe of the fan leading to the couloir, bottom up. We both almost decided to leave based off those results, but one we tried to reproduce with an ECT there was zero propagation observed. 

Awesome boot packing with a supportive layer below. Some sol…

reports.title: Cirque forepeak (north bowl attempt)
reports.comment: quick: The Day started Bluebird and calm up into the Alpine up until noon.  The snow on the south/east face was storm snow on top of a wind/sun crust 15cm down. We traversed Southeast with the plan to drop in from the south ridge to ski down 100M or so, then skin up to the saddle entrance to drop in the North bowl. Approaching the ridge the winds from the NW got stong, exposing a fair bit of bolde…

reports.title: crystal ridge
reports.comment: quick: Traversed crystal ridge yesterday on more of a ski-mo tour with little focus on skiing. Highly wind affected on the ridge top, with massive cornices overhanging the east side of the ridge. Had no evidence of cracking or instability, just some 2-4" slab on the surface in very small, isolated areas. Skied a few medium sized slopes as we traversed south along the ridge. Snow was heavy, crusty,…

reports.title: Noseeum Creek N Chutes
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the north facing bowl feature up the far end of Noseeum creek N Chutes. Snow was a little wind affected but still felt stable and skied pretty nicely.

We notice a size ~1.5ish slide up the top of the bowl through the choke. This looked like it was likely triggered by a cornice failure but it was hard to be 100% sure.

We opted against a second lap due to warming temps.

reports.title: Crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: Skied a variety of aspects between 1930m and 2270m, treeline and alpine features. 

On sunny slopes, the top 5cm of snow was sticky, heavy and moist (perfect snowball snow) by noon. 

Shady slopes stayed dry and the ski quality here was quite good with my skis penetrating 15-20cm in most places. 

Some wide-open and wind exposed slopes had  a nasty breakable wind skin (about 5cm thick) whic…

reports.title: Flower Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Dug two pits, one at treeline, one just under the couloir, both were solid, higher elevation showed better bonding.

Slight crust just under the new snow seemed to show signs of being a slab in isolated places, but was completely. nonreactive. 

Lots of sloughing on the ski down, resulting in a size 1 dry loose. We didnt ski the petals as we were low on time and werent certain of conditions…

reports.title: Crowfoot Shoots/Glades
reports.comment:
quick: 8-10cm fresh snow on top of sun crust. 
Found the match 24th crust (see attached photo)
First skied a shoot (on NNE aspect), then mellow to steep glades on second lap (NNW)

reports.title: Sugar Cube
reports.comment: quick: Mixed bag of conditions near cirque today. Mashed potatoes on solar aspects below 1900m by 1PM. Breakable melt-freeze/solar on East aspects to 2300m. Good skiing found where wind has deposited enough to cover the crust. Pit dug at the base of sugar cube: CT7 uneven break down 20 on fresh soft windslab. CT13M resistant planar down 50 on a facet interface. No propagation of either on ECT & st…

reports.title: FOD / Grand Daddy conditions
reports.comment: quick: Skied Funnel of Death today. Good snow conditions in the couloir in most spots. Lots of debris from the past 2 days on all fans but no slabs were triggered that we could see. No spindrift in the couloir either while we were there. Party of 2 was going up Grand Daddy when we were leaving. Snow in West Niles was a 5cm of fresh over MFCr over moist snow which made for tricky turns down. Last p…

reports.title: South Shoulder Chute
reports.comment:
quick: Obvious debris from previous days on solar aspects, as expected (see second photo). 
As noted by other parties, crust beneath new snow with isolated pockets of unreactive slabs. 
Sluff is moving fast but is small. 
Good skiing to be had in the shade.

reports.title: Grand Daddy Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Skin track and boot pack from previous day mostly covered. Descent tracks mostly covered with a few ruts here and there, otherwise good skiing. Some slow to medium sloughing, easily managed by turning out to the side.

reports.title: Pac Man Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Climbed above the choke point of Pac Man before we were stopped by facets and a mean looking convexity. A supportive crust made for a decent bootpack up until that point.
Like other couloirs in the area there are isolated pockets where small unreactive slabs have formed above the crust.
Sluff is moving very fast with enough energy to take a skier off their feet.

reports.title: Flower Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Skiied the flower couloir and petals yesterday, stem was pretty not great with a lot of hard snow and moguls above the choke. Towards the fan skiing improved vastly and great powder at the exit gully. Petals were in bad condition, fairly windswept and sunbaked with not much snow left. Shockingly there were pockets of powder still up there but always sitting on a crust. 

Compression test pr…

reports.title: Didn't Jimmy our way up the couliour but still a good day.
reports.comment: quick: Wet loose avi evidence on skiers up right side. Stayed towards the middle of the bowl and away from the walls. Cornice still above on skiers up left side.

reports.title: Party in Grand Daddy
reports.comment: quick: Skied Grand Daddy Couloir mid morning on Sunday, March 27th. 4 parties for a total of around 15 people skied between 11 and 1ish. Line was definitely skied recently (yesterday or Friday), pretty sluffy but very manageable. Climbing conditions were good, easy work and solid purchase on each step. Fan was crusty but okay, lower slopes/trees quite brutal (crust). Some isolated old wind loading…

reports.title: Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Turned around at the glacier whilst heading to Crowfoot due to bad visibility with clouds sitting on the summit. Felt much warmer than forecast throughout the day, particularly in the sun. Ski out through the moraines was decent, crusty but skiable enough. A few large cornice failures observed on solar aspects. Lots of large pinwheels and debris through the second canyon on exit.

reports.title: Busier than a one-armed bricklayer in Baghdad
reports.comment:
quick: First party of a few up Granddaddy this morning, warm temps with no wind and several cornices overhead had me sweating more than a nun in a strip club. Decided to start early ~715am and thankfully the sun never shone directly on the fan while we were up there. 

Stability was bomber however moguls are starting to form just below the split in the lower couloir. Still some light powder to be …

reports.title: Pinwheely good day in Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Toured up crowfoot glades and did some mellow slopes with sparse trees at the top. Dug a pit and saw a sun crust about 5 inches down and another big crust about half a meter deep. The powder was great until the afternoon where it started to get wet from the warm temps (about 4 C). Saw a few sluffs on the big wall west of the glades so we stayed well away from the wall. On the descent, there…

reports.title: Bow Summit Roadside
reports.comment:
quick: Skied both Jimmy Junior Bowl and Bow Summit Roadside. Both had a few centimeters of powder on top of a supportive crust.

Column test was done on the south edge of slide path that is open all the way to valley floor.

CTH22 Resistant Planer at 25cm and then CTH28 Sudden Drop at 90 cm. Total depth 130cm with the bottom 30cm 1.5-2mm rounded facets. Very sugary.

Snow surface -1’C, snow temper…

reports.title: Sugar Cube Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Skied sugar cube couloir Sunday. Rapped into the line and performed a belayed ski cut with no result. Very little wind affect on the line, snow was hard, and consolidated. A couple cm of soft snow on top made the skiing acceptable so we were quite happy with the day! 

Skinned up summit run back up and over the ridge. Top 2” of snow on summit run was heavier and wetter than the couloir but …

reports.title: Avalanche over Crowfoot Falls
reports.comment: avalanche: Avalanche came down in the mid-afternoon, we suspect it was a cornice failure that triggered a significant amount of loose dry snow to come down over Crowfoot Falls ice climb. It was at least 30 m wide but didn’t seem to trigger an avalanche on the slope below the cliffs from what we could see.

reports.title: Mosquito Creek Scorcher
reports.comment: quick: Rode ramp peak and half of quartzite on Tuesday. Great spring riding conditions, turned around on quartzite due to a shallow snow pack in places and warmer conditions than we expected. We saw lots of evidence of point releases on our way out of the valley, but no big slopes slid. Temperature reached 0 degrees in the alpine at around 2pm.

reports.title: SteezyStokes
reports.comment:
quick: Nice day up at bow summit. The 5-10 cm snowfall softened things up and made for some great skiing. 

We skied corner shoot. Overall snow was great above 2200 ish m, however, in the afternoon anything below that got pretty wet.

reports.title: Crowfoot Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Signs of recent sloughing/flushing (24hrs or longer) out of the Couloir could be observed from the parking lot. Lots of refrozen roller balls on the fan as well. 
We stopped just shy of the choke point, near the ice on climbers right as not enough cold cover moved in to shield the cornices above us from the sun. The skiing in the Couloir was amazing, cold, dry and very well bonded powder. A…

reports.title: Pac man
reports.comment:
quick: Attempted pac man couloir but turned around just above the choke. An easy result with a hand sheer test 30cm down gave concerns about the convex feature above the choke. Wind slab was prominent in the fan and couloir.

 Skied two laps from the fan down the north bowl to peyto lake. First lap the overnight freeze held well but by the time we were up for lap 2 the warmth had done its work and…

reports.title: Crowfoot Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Avi forecast is Low Low Low and observations supported that. Warm melt freeze created a solid crust.

Some debris from previous warm temps, but no movement today of any overhead snow or cornices. / weather: Wind blowing hard at mountain top. / snowpack: Initial compression test - top crust layer went after 3 from elbow.

Deep Compression Test. The 70 cm layer was sudden collapse after 1 arm…

reports.title: Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Summited crowfoot and skied from about 200m below summit. We saw almost everything weather wise but no rain. Conditions were stable. Snow was much better than expected.

reports.title: Bow Yoho Traverse
reports.comment:
quick: Jasper Visitor Safety Spent April 9-12, 2021 on the Bow to Yoho Traverse. 

Weather 
Over the 4 days the daytime highs were -10 and the overnight lows were -20. Skies where a mix of high overcast, convective clouds, and clear. Overnight on April 10 we had strong NE winds in the Alpine, other than that winds were light to moderate form the N with some easterly. We received only trace amounts…

reports.title: Grand Daddy Coulior
reports.comment: quick: Skied Grand Daddy on Wednesday. Temperature was well below zero (no warmer than -10 throughout the day) and the couloir had been heavily skied resulting in all the previous snow to form a hard crusty bumpy surface. Mainly survival skiing in spots at the top. The best skiing was in the fan below.

reports.title: Flower Couloir Area
reports.comment: quick: A nice day with good views at Flower Couloir. Two other groups climbed and skied at the same time as us. Conditions in the couloir were crusty, skied out and chunky. Difficult descent conditions. Some powder in the bowl below the petals, skied out and crusty in the upper chutes.

reports.title: Jimmy junior bowl
reports.comment: quick: Skied Jimmy junior bowl today. Ski quality was good with a 5-15cm of powder (depending on the area) on a hard supportive crust. Made for some fun fast powder laps. Old tracks and previous wet loose point releases made ski quality interesting in spots with rock hard chunks or inconsistency under the  new snow. Air temperature was around -10 but the snow temp was -5 and was increasing. Only s…

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: The cold nights and mild days have faceted out the near surface of the snow especially on north aspects and probably cornices too.  The new snow this week might bond poorly.  Great travel conditions on the lakes they are in perfect skate skiing condition. The slopes were a mix of powder and wind crust and sun crust with colouir and gullies type features holding the best snow. Generally abou…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Icy skin track conditions and a nasty breakable crust on all aspects made for an enjoyable day to just get outside. Surface snow was starting to warm up even on N/NW slopes at 2200m by 1:30pm. New snow from the past couple days wasn't enough to improve skiing over the breakable crust.

No new avalanche activity was observed.

reports.title: Flower coulior
reports.comment: avalanche: Skier accidental point release of storm snow from today. Avalanche moved fast and gained mass more quickly than expected.

reports.title: Noseeum W face
reports.comment: quick: Got an early start and headed up the W face of Noseeum mt this morning. Initially we felt dumb for waking up so early and where doubtful our line would warm up enough for the crusty conditions to improve at all. To our surprise we skinned the first half of the feature and only boot packed the top half which made things easier. At the top when we finally reached the sunshine we found some we…

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: Solid melt crust freeze made for fast and icy travel through the canyon to the wapta.

Excellent skiing was found off the summit, rapidly deteriorating to crusty shite below 2500m.

As the day got quite warm - fresh debris from numerous size 1s were observed in the canyon that were not present on the skin up.

reports.title: Grand Daddy Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Good coverage from the road and overnight freeze made for easy travel to base of the couloir. Ski crampons useful on the fan. Decent bootpacking. Small bits of snow periodically coming down from upper climbers right. But nothing alarming. Couloir skied OK. Mix of hard and soft snow. But not cement! Somewhat marginal conditions in the upper portion turned us around beneath the upper pillar. …

reports.title: Bow NE bowl
reports.comment: quick: Skied the more mellow NE bowl on bow peak. Access was quick other than getting up the last steep S slope to the top of the line. Ski crampons where 100% necessary and skinning was pretty brutal on the steeper slope. When we topped out on the ridge we ate some lunch and scoped our cornice guarded entry. We ended up just jumping off the cornice because the outrun and snow below looked great a…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Bow Summit: Snowpack test at 2223m, 11:00am, 3degrees, partly cloudy, on North-Facing slopes. Pencil crust, settled snowpack with large grains of snow. 

Moist under crust. Upper crust breaking and cracking under feet. By 1:00 saw evidence of many new wet loose slides on steeper slopes, and witnessed several from afar.

reports.title: Mt Weed
reports.comment:
quick: Great day climbing south face of Mt weed. Very good refreeze and 10-20 cm crust made skin travel quick. Tricky route finding below treeline but once in the Avalanche path its a straight shot up. / avalanche: Cross loaded Pockets of WSL on both sides of the couliour, exposed crust breaks continuity. Fairly touchy on top of the MFcr, easy to clean out. Best skiing was on the debris. 

Evidenc…

reports.title: Wapta 4 Peaks
reports.comment:
quick: Skied St.Nich, both summits of Olive and Gordon from bow lake on Sunday
- Lake crossing was fast with refreeze in the morning, but had 6-12 inches of water in the afternoon/evening overtop of the ice for most of it. Personally I wouldn't advise traveling at the end of the day for much longer or at all.
- Canyon had good coverage and en-route to bow hut only had to take skis off for a couple…

reports.title: Noseeum
reports.comment:
quick: Was going to do Cathedral but the lake O,'Hara road has  started to be plowed and there was no freeze at the parking lot.

Skied the south aspect of the west outlier of Noseeum as the snow looked the best.  We skied down at 1030 am but we were a couple hours early for good corn skiing.  The headwall was pretty much done for the season. Going up it was punchy to bootpacking but treacherous t…

reports.title: Bow summit roadside
reports.comment: quick: Quick lap up the avalanche paths past bow summit, one or two snow bridges left for the creek crossing. Snow was variable melt freeze crust with pockets of good snow and some fresh 5 to 10 cm building up. Stormy day out with Southerly wind picking up from moderate to strong and snow coming down heavily by noon with poor visibility.

reports.title: Sun effect at Bow summit
reports.comment: quick: Stable, consolidated snowpack aprox. 200cm in depth.  Some signs of avalanche debris from small releases, from earlier in the week. Snow conditions were a few cm on top of hard, mostly supportive suncrust.  Far from ideal conditions but great to be out in the mountains on a nice sunny day.  Parking lot at Bow Summit was a zoo with non-skiers out for the day.  Arguments and confrontations br…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr.
reports.comment: quick: The higher we went the less supportive the snow was but overall the skiing was pretty good. No complaints for July 2nd. Up to 1m+ of snow still in places, skiing is still on!
